questions.question: What is the most reliable source of genuine entrepreneurial opportunities according to this course?

options.text: Reading business bestsellers and copying their ideas
Identifying real, unmet problems experienced by a specific group of people
Choosing the most fashionable industry trend of the year
Launching a product that already has many competitors

questions.explanation: Genuine opportunities arise from clearly defined problems faced by real people. Solving a specific, unmet need creates sustainable competitive advantage.

questions.question: How does a 'problem' differ from an 'opportunity' in the entrepreneurial context?

options.text: Problems are always negative and opportunities are always positive
An opportunity is a problem that has been validated as worth solving and is addressable by a viable business
They are the same thing — all problems are immediately business opportunities
Opportunities exist only in technology sectors; problems exist everywhere

questions.explanation: A problem becomes an entrepreneurial opportunity when there is a significant target market, willingness to pay, and a feasible solution that can be delivered as a business.

questions.question: Which of the following domains is mentioned as offering significant entrepreneurial opportunities in India?

options.text: Only information technology
Healthcare, agriculture, education, fintech, and clean energy among others
Only sectors where no existing companies operate
Only government-regulated industries

questions.explanation: India presents vast entrepreneurial opportunities across healthcare, agritech, edtech, fintech, clean energy, and many other domains due to gaps in access, quality, and affordability.

questions.question: According to the guest session on AI, which aspect of AI is most directly relevant for entrepreneurs identifying new opportunities?

options.text: The ability to replace all human workers immediately
AI as a tool to enhance productivity and create new product categories
AI as a replacement for entrepreneurial creativity and judgment
AI-generated business plans that require no human validation

questions.explanation: AI is a powerful enabling technology that entrepreneurs can use to enhance productivity, personalise offerings, and create entirely new product categories, rather than a replacement for human judgment.

questions.question: The healthcare guest session highlights which key challenge as an entrepreneurial opportunity in India?

options.text: Excess supply of qualified doctors in rural areas
Gaps in healthcare accessibility, affordability, and quality especially in underserved regions
Over-digitalisation of patient records
Absence of any government healthcare scheme

questions.explanation: India faces significant gaps in healthcare access and quality, particularly in Tier 2/3 cities and rural areas, creating large addressable markets for health-tech entrepreneurs.

questions.question: What is a key technique for identifying entrepreneurial opportunities from personal experience?

options.text: Only observing what large companies are building
Identifying pain points and frustrations in everyday life
Randomly brainstorming products without any user research
Selecting sectors purely based on stock market performance

questions.explanation: Many successful startups originate from founders who personally experienced a problem. Noticing friction points in daily life is a powerful opportunity identification technique.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why the same problem can create different opportunities in different contexts?

options.text: Because problems have no universal solutions and context determines viability
Because all problems have exactly one correct solution
Because problems are identical across all geographies
Because opportunities are independent of available technology

questions.explanation: The same problem can yield different viable solutions depending on local infrastructure, regulatory environment, customer behaviour, technology availability, and willingness to pay.

questions.question: When evaluating a potential entrepreneurial opportunity, which criterion is LEAST important at the idea stage?

options.text: Size of the addressable market
Existence of a genuine customer pain point
Exact final logo and brand name of the company
Founder's ability to build or access the solution

questions.explanation: At the idea stage, market size, customer pain, and founder capability matter most. Branding details like logos are execution elements that come much later in the process.
